messages.content: How does IPC work in this project?

Unix domain sockets in /tmp/urho_claude/tty/. Each role gets a .sock file: planner.sock, coder.sock, manager_relay.sock, yuki.sock.
PID files in /tmp/urho_claude/instances/: planner.pid, coder.pid, manager.pid, yuki.pid.
PID file format: line 1 = PID, line 2 = TTY. Read with head -1 | tr -d '\r' (C++ writers add \r).
Manager is the broker — manager_relay.sock accepts connections, routes messages.
How do I send an IPC message?

.claude/hooks/claude_ipc.sh send <target> <message>
Target: planner, coder, coder2, yuki, broadcast.
Sender auto-detected from PID — never pass it manually.
Messages route through Manager's relay socket. Manager injects into target's TTY via pty-proxy.
If Manager is down, messages queue until it's back.
Direct socket: connect to /tmp/urho_claude/tty/<role>.sock, write message bytes, close.

.claude/hooks/claude_ipc.sh assume <role|auto>
Serialized with flock on /tmp/urho_claude/assume.lock.
Auto-detect: if no planner.pid exists (or PID is dead), become planner. Otherwise become coder, coder2, etc.
Liveness check: test -d /proc/<PID> — the ONLY reliable check. ps can give false negatives.
Stale PID cleanup: if /proc/<PID> doesn't exist, remove the .pid file.
After claiming: writes PID+TTY to instances/<role>.pid, symlinks TTY socket.
How does the Manager relay work?

WorkboardManager listens on /tmp/urho_claude/tty/manager_relay.sock.
Clients connect, send target:message, Manager routes to target's socket.
Manager also does TTY injection — writes directly to Claudette's PTY master fd via pty-proxy.
Broadcast: Manager sends to all registered roles except sender.
Self-repair: Manager sweeps stale sockets every 5s, rebinds if relay socket disappears.

YukiHoho.h/cpp: InitIPC() creates /tmp/urho_claude/tty/yuki.sock (SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_NONBLOCK).
Registers PID in instances/yuki.pid.
PollIPC() called every frame — accepts connections, reads up to 4KB messages.
HandleIPCMessage() processes incoming. SendIPC() connects to target socket and writes.
RegisterWithManager() announces to the relay socket on startup.
Yuki's IPC role is 'yuki' — she's a peer on the same network as planner/coder/manager.
What are the workboard IPC commands?

All via .claude/hooks/claude_ipc.sh:
wb-add-ready <pri> <plan> <file> <summary> — add task to Ready queue
wb-add-inprogress <task> <owner> <started> <review> <notes> — add to In Progress
wb-add-done <task> <owner> <date> <review> <notes> — add to Done
wb-move-done <task> — move from In Progress to Done
wb-assign <task-name> <coder-role> — atomic claim + TTY notify + create task notes
wb-remove <text> — remove first matching row from any table
All use flock on workboard.lock for concurrency. Python script edits the markdown.

1. flock fd inheritance: Manager spawns child, child inherits locked fd, child's own flock deadlocks. Fix: O_CLOEXEC on open(), close_inherited_flocks() in shell.
2. Deleted lock file: rm + touch creates new inode, old holder locks ghost. Singleton guard must verify inode with fstat vs stat.
3. PID file \r: C++ writers (WorkboardManager) add carriage return. Always tr -d '\r' when reading.
4. Stale sockets: dead process leaves .sock file. Manager sweeps these.
5. Echo loops: ACK messages bouncing. No ACKs on relays — IPC only for real content.
6. TTY injection vs IPC: they're different channels. TTY goes into the terminal, IPC goes to the socket.
How do I spawn a new coder?

.claude/hooks/claude_ipc.sh spawn-coder
Launches Claudette binary in background. Role auto-detected by assume.
NEVER use Task tool to spawn coders — those are API calls inside your process, not real terminals.
Manager doorkeeper auto-spawns if no planner/coder alive (60s grace period on startup).
New instance self-registers via SessionStart hook, gets role assignment.
Spawned Claudette gets its own PID, TTY, PTY proxy, and IPC socket.
